idiom_name: dup/clone copy plus rebinding of a frozen value
implementation_notes: Ruby objects are references and = rebinds, so the pattern becomes the copy-then-publish discipline: copy the receiver (dup for a shallow unfrozen copy, clone to keep the singleton class and the frozen state, overriding initialize_copy to customise either), apply the change to the copy, and publish it with one assignment. Freezing the published value (#freeze) makes in-place mutation an error rather than a convention, and frozen value objects (Data.define, frozen Structs, frozen collections) play the role the immutable case class plays elsewhere. Where an in-place commit is genuinely required -- identity matters, or a shared reference must observe the change -- the replace-style APIs (String#replace, Array#replace, Hash#replace) install a fully built value into the existing object in one call, which is Ruby's closest equivalent to the non-throwing swap.
code_sketch:
class Cart
  attr_reader :items
  def initialize(items = []) = @items = items.freeze

  def with_item(item) = Cart.new(@items + [item]).freeze   # complete copy first
end

cart = cart.with_item(item)      # publish by rebinding; the old cart is untouched

pitfalls: dup and clone are shallow and differ: clone keeps the frozen state and the singleton class, dup does not, so frozen.clone.modify! raises while frozen.dup.modify! succeeds -- pick deliberately and re-freeze the copy if it must be edited.

Copying does not run the constructor: initialize_copy/initialize_dup hooks decide what a copy is, and validation or normalisation performed in initialize is silently skipped unless the hook redoes it (or the copy goes through a new instance).

A frozen object's contents are not frozen: frozen_array << x, frozen_hash[k] = v and frozen_string << 'x' all mutate the referenced object, so deep immutability needs frozen elements (or a deep_freeze).
Copy-then-publish is not atomic with respect to other threads: the GVL does not make a read-modify-write sequence safe, so shared state still needs a Mutex or a concurrent structure around the swap.
